title: Je t'aime, Andréa  (I Love You, Andréa)

segments.t: Outside the crowded Cannes party, Andrea receives an unexpected phone call from Colette. Just as their heartfelt conversation concludes, Gabriel stumbles over in tears with heartbreaking news. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Je suis désolée pour hier soir.
Ce n'est pas facile pour toi.
Je voulais te dire que je suis là.
Je veux le vivre avec toi.
Let's walk through these two emotional phone and party moments step by step.
'Hello, Colette?' Again that phone-specific 'hello' opens Andrea's call with rising pitch as she checks who is on the line in French.
Je suis désolée pour hier soir.
'I am sorry about last night.' Literally 'yesterday evening'—French never says 'last night' for the evening hours before midnight!
'I really crossed the line.' Literally 'passed beyond the boundary-stones,' a vivid French idiom from ancient stone markers for going too far!
'No, it is nothing.' Reassuring 'it is nothing' in the negative is a handy phrase to brush off a small slight in French.
Ce n'est pas facile pour toi.
'It is not easy for you.' Simple 'it is not easy' pairs with emphatic 'for you' at the end word for word.
'You are living through something incredible.' Again after 'something,' French requires 'of' before the description—literally 'something of incredible.'
Je voulais te dire que je suis là.
'I wanted to tell you that I am here.' Softening 'want' into ongoing past 'wanted' makes Colette's reassurance extra tender in French.
Je veux le vivre avec toi.
'I want to experience it with you.' In French, 'live it' covers 'experience it' or 'go through it,' with 'it' placed right before 'live.'
'Because I love you, Andrea.' Two-word 'because' introduces 'I you love'—since French always puts 'you' ahead of 'love'!
'I love you too, Colette.' Leading with 'me too' at the very front is how French makes 'I love you too' warm and emphatic.
'Sofia is gone!' Motion 'left/gone' takes 'is' as its helper in French and adds a silent '-e' matching Sofia.
'She definitely left me.' Careful false friend: in French, 'definitively' means 'for good' or 'permanently,' not 'definitely'!
'She was completely right.' Past-tense 'she had totally reason' turns the classic 'have reason' expression into 'she was right.'
'I really am a piece of trash!' Literally 'garbage/refuse,' a harsh French self-insult when someone feels like a total scoundrel.

'Gabriel, calm down a little.' Hyphenated 'calm-yourself' followed by 'a little' is the gentlest everyday way to soothe a friend in French. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Je suis désolée pour hier soir.
Ce n'est pas facile pour toi.
Je voulais te dire que je suis là.
Je veux le vivre avec toi.
After receiving an unexpected and heartfelt confession of love from Colette, Andrea turns to comfort a devastated Gabriel after Sofia leaves him. See you next time!

lines.fragment: Je suis désolé pour hier soir
Je sais que c'est pas facile pour toi en ce moment
Je voulais juste te dire que je suis là
Et je crois que je veux le vivre avec toi
